title: Plugins and dynamic loading: the real limits of the approach

videos.script: This is the last lesson of the course, and the last of four escape hatches. Reflection, unsafe and cgo each bought something and sent a bill. Plugins do the same. {{plugin}} A Go plugin is a package compiled on its own into a shared object. A running program opens it, finds a variable or a function by name, and calls it. The hits tool gets two reporters this way: one writes CSV, the other prints a mean. {{breaks}} Then the bill. The program and the plugin must be built from the same source, with the same flags and the same Go. Add one method to a shared package, and the plugin refuses to load. Nothing can be unloaded. And it works on Linux, macOS and FreeBSD, with cgo, and nowhere else. {{alternatives}} So, two other ways to add a reporter. A separate program that reads JSON and writes text, in any language, where a crash stays outside. And reporters compiled into the binary and chosen by name, the way database drivers are. {{choosing}} Last, the three side by side, with measured numbers: what a call costs, what has to ship, and what breaks. Then the course ends where it started, with hits.
